messages:
maya-ng: Heads up — the role_hierarchy migration canary in prod failed during assign step. Started seeing 502s from auth-service when assigning the default role to new accounts. :warning:

alex-w: Any error logs? which shard/region?

maya-ng: Canary ran in us-west1, job id migration-2026-03-10-13:45. Pasting the failing trace:```
Error: duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"role_uid_key\"
  at SQL: INSERT INTO role_assignments (uid, role_id, created_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)
  at migration runner/migrate.go:142
```

infra-bot: migration-2026-03-10-13:45 exited with status 1. Retry count: 3. Logged at 2026-03-10T13:46:01Z.

samir: Looks like the backfill isn't idempotent — concurrent canary workers might be inserting the same role uid. Use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING or a dedupe pre-check. Also check that role_uid is globally unique across legacy and new schema.

alex-w: We should not blast a global ON CONFLICT blindly — that hides other logic. Plan: 1) identify dup source, 2) dedupe in-place with a migration that merges duplicates, 3) make insert idempotent.

maya-ng: Found root cause: old system allowed multiple role_assignments for same uid when imported from legacy CSVs. Canary attempted to create normalized single row and hit existing duplicates created earlier by ad-hoc imports.

olivia-s: Related question — does the migration runner need KMS decrypt access for the role_salt column? Audit shows a KMS permission error around the same time for serviceAccount:migration-runner@redwood-svc.

maya-ng: Good catch. The runner tries to decrypt role_salt to compute canonical uid. If decrypt fails we fallback to raw value, which produced inconsistent canonicalization and duplicate keys. Audit snippet:```
logName: projects/REDACTED/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access
protoPayload.serviceName: cloudkms.googleapis.com
protoPayload.methodName: projects.locations.keyRings.keys.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricDecrypt
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: migration-runner@redwood-svc
protoPayload.status.code: 7
```

olivia-s: So two issues: missing KMS permission causing wrong canonical uid, and legacy duplicate rows. We should fix perms first to stabilize canary.

alex-w: Proposed immediate actions:```
1) Pause further canaries (set canary_percent=0).
2) Grant migration-runner minimal KMS decrypt role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the key.
3) Run a dedupe job in staging and run a small deterministic merge in prod canary (10 users).
4) Ensure migration insert uses ON CONFLICT (role_uid) DO UPDATE SET role_id = EXCLUDED.role_id (explicit merge logic).
```

samir: SQL for safe dedupe (staging):```sql
-- find duplicates
SELECT role_uid, array_agg(id) AS ids, count(*) AS cnt
FROM role_assignments
GROUP BY role_uid
HAVING count(*) > 1;

-- merge plan: keep smallest id, reassign references, delete others
WITH dups AS (
  SELECT role_uid, min(id) AS keep_id, array_agg(id) AS all_ids
  FROM role_assignments
  GROUP BY role_uid
  HAVING count(*) > 1
)
UPDATE references r
SET role_assignment_id = d.keep_id
FROM dups d
WHERE r.role_assignment_id = ANY(d.all_ids) AND r.role_assignment_id <> d.keep_id;

DELETE FROM role_assignments ra
USING dups d
WHERE ra.role_uid = d.role_uid AND ra.id <> d.keep_id;
```

maya-ng: +1. We'll run dedupe in staging tomorrow at 05:00 UTC and run a 10-user canary after.

olivia-s: KMS fix: to grant decrypt, run (replace placeholders):```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/role-secrets/cryptoKeys/role-key \
  --member=serviceAccount:migration-runner@redwood-svc \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
I'll coordinate with infra to apply and add a short-lived audit scope so we can revert.

oncall-rotation: tagging @oncall to monitor for regressions post-retry. If we see >5% 5xx in auth-service revert to previous canary snapshot.

alex-w: Also update the migration runner to log when decrypt fails and include the raw fallback value for traceability. Don't swallow the error.

samir: Long-term: add a preflight that compares canonical uid distribution between legacy and new logic and fail the run if divergence > 0.5%. That will catch silent KMS/method changes.

maya-ng: Decision: pause rollout, fix KMS perms, run dedupe in staging, deploy idempotent migration change, then resume canary at 10% for an hour and monitor costs + 5xx. If clean, do progressive rollout 10->25->50->100.

olivia-s: I'll apply the KMS binding now and post the audit entry. ETA 10m.

maya-ng: Thanks — tagging this thread for postmortem notes. We'll capture root cause (legacy duplicates + missing kms decrypt) and list remediation steps. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Action recorded: migration-paused by maya-ng at 2026-03-10T13:55:20Z. Audit link: https://console.re/redwood/audit/REDACTED

alex-w: After KMS is fixed, run a dry-run with 1 user to validate canonical uid is stable before dedupe.

maya-ng: Agreed. I'll follow up with results in this thread.
